sourceChecks.claim: Caching benefits repeated reads and repeated computation by reusing stored results; the source remains the persistent repository.
The application checks the cache, reads the source on a miss, adds the result, and returns it; cache-aside does not guarantee consistency.
Application logic implements cache-aside; structured keys distinguish different cached values.
Updating the source then invalidating the cached entry is the cache-aside write pattern, and consistency is not guaranteed.
Memory-based eviction follows configured policies including LRU; noeviction rejects commands caching new data.
Independent local caches can contain different versions; external caches share values but add operational and availability considerations.
Coalescing reduces simultaneous duplicate source requests; cache outages can overwhelm dependencies unless fallback is capped or load is shed.
Usage patterns, volatility, performance analysis, and synchronization costs determine whether caching is appropriate.
